title: A Current That Light Can Use Up

scenes.tts: Your eyes work in starlight and in bright sun. How can one kind of cell cope with both?
scenes.visual: Title card: A Current That Light Can Use Up. A night sky beside a sunlit field. Question on screen: how can one cell cope with both?
scenes.narration: Your eyes work in starlight and in bright sun. How can one kind of cell cope with both?

scenes.tts: Between starlight and sunlight, the light changes a hundred-million-fold or more.
scenes.visual: A long logarithmic light scale from a star icon to a sun icon. Label: a hundred-million-fold or more (10^8).
scenes.narration: Between starlight and sunlight, the light changes a hundred-million-fold or more.

scenes.tts: Yet a dark-adapted rod goes from barely responding to saturated over about a hundredfold range of flashes.
scenes.visual: Below the long scale, a short bracket spanning about two decades of flash strength. Flash responses grow from tiny to a flat ceiling. Label: dark-adapted rod, roughly a hundredfold.
scenes.narration: Yet a dark-adapted rod goes from barely responding to saturated over about a hundredfold range of flashes.

scenes.tts: In darkness, c G M P holds channels open in the outer segment. A steady dark current flows in.
scenes.caption: In darkness, cGMP holds channels open in the outer segment. A steady dark current flows in.
scenes.visual: Zoom into a rod outer segment. Channels in the outer-segment membrane held open by cGMP dots. Inward arrows of current. A filled bar beside the cell, labelled current still flowing. Label: dark current.
scenes.narration: In darkness, cGMP holds channels open in the outer segment. A steady dark current flows in.

scenes.tts: Light activates P D E, which breaks down c G M P, and channels close. Each response switches off part of that current.
scenes.caption: Light activates PDE, which breaks down cGMP, and channels close. Each response switches off part of that current.
scenes.visual: A light flash activates PDE; cGMP dots vanish, some channels close, inward arrows thin. The current bar drops by a chunk.
scenes.narration: Light activates PDE, which breaks down cGMP, and channels close. Each response switches off part of that current.

scenes.tts: So light spends the current. What is still flowing limits how big the next response can be.
scenes.visual: The current bar alone, labelled current still flowing: room for the next response. Light arrows lower it.
scenes.narration: So light spends the current. What is still flowing limits how big the next response can be.

scenes.tts: Two terms. Gain is how much current one absorbed photon switches off, and for how long.
scenes.visual: Definition card: gain = current one photon switches off, and for how long. A single small dip in the current trace.
scenes.narration: Two terms. Gain is how much current one absorbed photon switches off, and for how long.

scenes.tts: Sensitivity is the response to a dim flash, divided by the strength of that flash.
scenes.visual: Definition card: sensitivity = response to a dim flash, divided by flash strength.
scenes.narration: Sensitivity is the response to a dim flash, divided by the strength of that flash.

scenes.tts: Predict. Suppose a rod's gain never changed. What would a modest steady background do to it?
scenes.visual: A rod with a lock icon labelled fixed gain. A steady background light switches on. Question on screen: what happens?
scenes.narration: Predict. Suppose a rod's gain never changed. What would a modest steady background do to it?

scenes.tts: It would close nearly every channel. The rod would be saturated, unable to signal any further brightening. Only dimming the light would let current return.
scenes.visual: The current bar drops almost to empty. A brighter test flash arrives and the trace stays nearly flat. Label: saturated for increments.
scenes.narration: It would close nearly every channel. The rod would be saturated, unable to signal any further brightening. Only dimming the light would let current return.

scenes.tts: So a photoreceptor turns its own gain down as the background brightens.
scenes.visual: Split screen. Left: fixed-gain cell, bar empty, flat test response. Right: a cell with a dial turning its gain down.
scenes.narration: So a photoreceptor turns its own gain down as the background brightens.

scenes.tts: Calcium feedback helps. While the light stays on, it reopens some channels, keeping current in reserve.
scenes.visual: Right panel: some channels reopen and the current bar partly refills. Label: current in reserve.
scenes.narration: Calcium feedback helps. While the light stays on, it reopens some channels, keeping current in reserve.

scenes.tts: It also cuts and shortens each new response. Each photon does less.
scenes.visual: Right panel: a test flash gives a smaller, briefer dip, but a clear one. Label: lower gain.
scenes.narration: It also cuts and shortens each new response. Each photon does less.

scenes.tts: The result is called Weber behaviour. On brighter backgrounds, sensitivity falls roughly as one over the background.
scenes.visual: A log-log plot of sensitivity against background: flat near the dark value at dim backgrounds, then bending onto a line approaching slope minus one. Label: Weber behaviour, written once.
scenes.narration: The result is called Weber behaviour. On brighter backgrounds, sensitivity falls roughly as one over the background.

scenes.tts: Contrast is a change in light, as a fraction of the background.
scenes.visual: Definition card: contrast = change in light as a fraction of the background. A brief flash drawn on a background level.
scenes.narration: Contrast is a change in light, as a fraction of the background.

scenes.tts: The payoff. On bright backgrounds, take small, brief flashes of the same contrast and the same duration. Their photon count grows with the background, while sensitivity falls just as fast. So their peak responses stay about the same.
scenes.visual: Three bright backgrounds a decade apart, each with the same small, brief 10% flash of the same duration T. On screen: fixed contrast C and duration T; I well above I0 (the half-sensitivity point); flash photons = C × I × T; sensitivity falls as 1/I; peak response ≈ S(I) × C × I × T. Below each, peak responses of about the same height.
scenes.narration: The payoff. On bright backgrounds, take small, brief flashes of the same contrast and the same duration. Their photon count grows with the background, while sensitivity falls just as fast. So their peak responses stay about the same.

scenes.tts: Now remove the G caps. In darkness, a rod's response to one photon gets larger.
scenes.visual: A cell with the GCAP arrow crossed out. In darkness its single-photon dip is larger.
scenes.narration: Now remove the GCAPs. In darkness, a rod's response to one photon gets larger.
scenes.caption: Now remove the GCAPs. In darkness, a rod's response to one photon gets larger.

scenes.tts: But on a background it keeps less current in reserve. Its sensitivity falls more steeply.
scenes.visual: The log-log plot again: a second curve that falls more steeply than the Weber line. Label: GCAP feedback absent; other recovery mechanisms remain.
scenes.narration: But on a background it keeps less current in reserve. Its sensitivity falls more steeply.

scenes.tts: This picture comes mainly from mouse rods and cones. A bright enough light can still saturate them.
scenes.visual: Small scope note on screen: mouse rods and cones, ex vivo; feedback extends the range but has limits.
scenes.narration: This picture comes mainly from mouse rods and cones. A bright enough light can still saturate them.

scenes.tts: Pigment bleaching, light using up visual pigment, and other mechanisms extend the range in bright light.
scenes.visual: Scope note continues: bleaching and other mechanisms extend the range in bright light.
scenes.narration: Pigment bleaching, light using up visual pigment, and other mechanisms extend the range in bright light.

scenes.tts: One feedback loop does most of this work. The test is to cut it.
scenes.visual: A calcium loop drawn faintly, with a pair of scissors hovering over it.
scenes.narration: One feedback loop does most of this work. The test is to cut it.

scenes.tts: The takeaway. Light spends a limited current, and calcium feedback keeps some in reserve.
scenes.visual: Takeaway card: the current bar, part spent and part held in reserve, with a calcium arrow holding the reserve open.
scenes.narration: The takeaway. Light spends a limited current, and calcium feedback keeps some in reserve.
